title: My fine-tuned AI Trading Model after three weeks
author: Must_Dragonfruit
selftext:
I fine-tuned it with a 45GB corpus. Running on its own VM with IBKR gateway. 

https://preview.redd.it/b8vbetdsd88h1.png?width=1170&format=png&auto=webp&s=5e4e2f82b087f183f937ffc007aa7dc9398c2fec

comments.author: flav0rc0untry
comments.body: I think this stuff is interesting. Can you elaborate on what tools your using and the using and your process

replies.author: Must_Dragonfruit
replies.body:
Sure, I have 15 years of trading experience, so I trained the AI model on that data. 

After that, I gave it its own Azure instance running on an Nvidia GPU and let it loose... 

IBKR's API is very complicated, it took me several days to get it working and it still flakes out every so often... I'm looking into Alpaca next but their market data really sucks.

replies.author: Terese08150815
replies.body: If you need high quality data, try amberdata. not cheap. i pay for binance futures api 600$ / month. But you get the real data from the platform you work with or want to work with.

replies.author: maddog107
replies.body: Massive has great market data. The price isn’t to bad and it’s good quality data

replies.author: vitholomewjenkins
replies.body: I do options and I’m trying out tastytrade and tradier. So far, tradier API is more consistent (and simplified)  than tastytrade. Hope you keep us updated.

replies.author: mdawe1
replies.body: Switch to IBKR websocket less flakey

replies.author: Must_Dragonfruit
replies.body:
will do!

mainly I hate the 2FA requirement every week. Can't seem to get around that.

replies.author: flav0rc0untry
replies.body: Are there any good educational resources you can recommend

replies.author: Must_Dragonfruit
replies.body:
if you can share your plan, i can give you some ideas on where to go... 

I've been working on this concept for several months and finally was able to put it together. 

The performance is surprising, I really expected 3% which is what my modeling had predicted.

comments.author: mrfunkm
comments.body: Looks good, interested in your hardware requirements here. Also with IBKR, are you paying for live data? I’ve tried running the gateway on a docker container and it has a daily wobble in the early hours, hence moving to alpaca, I’m paper trading btw

replies.author: Must_Dragonfruit
replies.body:
I am paying for live data. It’s not expensive although technically it doesn’t need it. 

I had to give ibkr its own vm on azure + an nvidia gpu for the AI model.  It costs me about a $200 a month or so not including training costs.

comments.author: ThatEmploy7
comments.body: Can you say something about what you input to your model and what it outputs?

replies.author: Must_Dragonfruit
replies.body:
I don’t input anything. I trained it to think like me based on my data and then gave it access to all the market data.  It picks stocks on a long term basis and rebalances monthly. 

Basically i made a financial advisor. Me + a lot more knowledge of technical factors and quantitative info from SEC on companies.

comments.author: BobtheGodGamer
comments.body: How much did the training cost? What model did you use as the base?

replies.author: Must_Dragonfruit
replies.body:
I run several other workloads on AWS, but I think it was around $600 or so. 

I mixed Qwen and DeepSeek and then finetuned using QLoRA.  

I am working on v2, day trading, super hard, over 100 approaches have failed, but that one i will put on GLM 5.2 once I can raise a cluster in Azure and once it can beat SPY.

replies.author: Must_Dragonfruit
replies.body:
I put the v2 candidates online at [https://engo.capital](https://engo.capital) 

check them out 😄 

If you have any ideas, please keep me posted.

comments.author: parthnaik
comments.body:
Nice work! I have been meaning to get into options trading using AI. I have built AI for environmental market predictions but those prices change only few times a week. I have a few questions:

1. Where can I get cheap historical data that can be used for back testing?
2. Would you recommend any back testing framework?
3. Would you recommend any pre-existing quant trading frameworks?
4. Do you have any book / resources recommendations that can help me?
4. If you have any other advice

replies.author: Must_Dragonfruit
replies.body:
you can go on my site, i have links to all the papers I used... 

historical data is tough.. you just have to burn tokens and pull them from the SEC or suck it up and pay... there are a ton of sites offering the data

I'm thinking of letting other people create their own strategies... and paper trade... you can visit it at [engo.capital](http://engo.capital)
